title: Janapada of Kamboja
capsule: Kamboja was one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas of Iron Age northern India, located on the northwestern frontier — roughly the region between Kabul and Kandahar in present-day Afghanistan — and attested in late Vedic sources from around 600 BCE. An Iranian-speaking people akin to Younger Avestan speakers, the Kambojas were famed horse breeders whose mounts were prized for warfare, and their capital Rajapura remains unlocated archaeologically. By around 500 BCE the region had been absorbed into the Achaemenid Empire under Cyrus the Great, and Kambojas appear by name in Darius I's Behistun Inscription and later in Ashoka's Fifth Rock Edict alongside Gandharians and Greeks. The kingdom left no surviving inscriptions of its own; knowledge depends entirely on Sanskrit epics, Pali texts, and Achaemenid imperial records.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested; no archaeological boundary markers survive, and ancient textual references place Kamboja only vaguely in the northwest, making any polygon reconstruction speculative.
